observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a full-height mirror wall on the left, draped teal curtains, a wooden ballet barre, and a pale wood floor. A woman in a pink long-sleeve top, black wide-leg trousers, and a white hair accessory stands on the floor; her mirror image appears on the left as a reflection of the same person, not a second dancer.
visible_changes: At the start (t=0) the woman is bent forward at the waist, one arm curved near her head and the other reaching down toward her foot, legs in a split/lunge stance; this posture is already in progress at the crop boundary.
Over t=0 to ~t=0.4 she straightens her torso and lifts both arms into a rounded overhead position while rotating her body toward the mirror side.
From ~t=0.5 to ~t=0.9 she rises onto one leg, extending the free leg backward and lifting both arms outward into a V, holding an arabesque/attitude-like pose.
Between ~t=0.9 and ~t=1.6 she sustains the one-leg pose with arms raised; the raised back leg alternates between a more extended and a more bent (attitude) position, and her head tilts back.
From ~t=1.6 to ~t=2.0 she lowers the back leg to the floor, brings her arms down to a forward horizontal position, and turns her body so her back faces the camera more directly.

From ~t=2.0 to the end (t=2.76) she walks steadily across the floor away from the mirror, arms relaxed at her sides, ending with her back to the camera still mid-stride; the walk is ongoing at the crop boundary.
The mirror reflection tracks each of these changes in real time, confirming it is the same person's image rather than a separate object.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the woman was doing before the forward-bent posture at t=0, and where her walk leads after t=2.76, are not shown.
The music, intent, or any cue that initiated the sequence is not visible.
uncertain_details: The camera appears largely static (background curtains, mirror seams, and barre hold fixed screen positions), but slight handheld drift cannot be ruled out.
Specific dance terminology (arabesque vs. attitude, etc.) is inferred from posture only; exact style names are not verifiable from the frames.
